Creates a public key from 32 bytes.

Current-behavior compatibility note: the current implementation retains the input array, and toByteArray exposes that same array. If those bytes are mutated after toBase58 or hashCode has populated its cache, the cached representation can disagree with the current bytes; two equal keys can then have different hash codes, contrary to hashCode. This is retained pending an owner decision.
Decodes a <METHOD> key from ASCII text held in a byte array, e.g. a raw JSON or wire buffer.

Finds Solana's canonical program address by trying bump seeds from 255 through 1.
The generated bump counts toward MAX_SEEDS, so callers may provide at most
15 seeds.

Derives an off-curve account from a base key, an ASCII seed, and a program id.

The returned asciiSeed contains the US-ASCII encoding of {@code baseSeed} followed by the selected nonce byte. Non-ASCII characters use Java's standard US-ASCII replacement byte. Nonces are tried from 127 through 0.

Derives a system-program address from a base, UTF-8 seed, and owner program id.

This follows Solana's {@code Address:: limit is measured in UTF-8 bytes, and an owner ending in the program-derived-address marker is illegal.

Returns this implementation's <METHOD>. Implementations may differ in whether that array
is shared; keys returned by createPubKey currently expose their backing
array, as described by that factory's cache-coherence compatibility note.

Verifies UTF-8 encodings of both arguments.
